What equipment did you use to produce this music?

Glad you like it! It's a unique style, it's not for everyone of course, but I'm glad you developed an appreciation for it. I made it using my Korg MS-2000 keyboard and a Korg Kaosillator Pro, and then feed it all in to a 4-channel looper pedal called "The Boomerang III Phrase Sampler". Then as I play, I record the output from the looper (which goes to the speakers) to the computer. I don't do any editing on the computer except volume and length, no software after-effects or anything. After I made about 100 songs, I decided I should select the best and release an album, and here it is! :)

Glad to see that Calgary police are responding so quickly to calls.

I've actually gone on a 13 hour ride along with them, it was really fascinating to see how they operate. In our downtown core there's always units driving around, so if there's a call they'll see it pop up on a map and all units in the area will head towards it (unless they're on another call), and the booking jail is downtown so units are never far away.
How did you go about hooking that up?

Ride alongs are usually meant for people interested in becoming an officer or going into some kind of law enforcement. The way to do it is to contact a local district office and ask how to fill out the ride along form, where to get it, etc. I am not pursuing a career with law enforcement, but I have a popular twitter account here in Calgary and contacted them asking if I could do a ride along and live-tweet it, which surprisingly came back as a yes. Here's the pics/info from it if you're interested http://crackmacs.ca/index.php/2014/10/ride-along-calgary-police/ -- wish I could do it again.
